item.title: A crystalline uranium Fischer-type carbyne
item.headline: A uranium–carbon bond stretches the meaning of “triple”
item.summary: Researchers isolated a crystalline molecule with an unusual uranium–carbon bonding pattern. Its three bonding components differ from a conventional triple bond; the study establishes fundamental chemistry, not an application.

evidence.question: Can a uranium Fischer-type carbyne be isolated and characterized?
evidence.method: Combined oxygen-free synthesis, X-ray crystallography, spectroscopy, magnetic measurements and electronic-structure calculations.
evidence.limitations: Bond labels simplify delocalized electron density; calculated bond order is about 1.2, not three.

explainer.finding: The evidence supports carbon donating an electron pair to uranium, with uranium returning two single-electron contributions in perpendicular directions.
explainer.method: Measured structure and electron-density analysis supported the calculated bonding picture; bond length alone was insufficient.
explainer.meaning: Drawing three lines between atoms can conceal different electron arrangements. Here, three principal bonding components do not mean three equally strong electron-pair bonds.
explainer.limits: Reaction tests remain preliminary, with some products unidentified. The work does not demonstrate a useful catalyst.
